title: Analysis
description: The complete set of Facts produced from one Program on one Python version.

pythonVersion.description: The version of the Python that produced this Analysis, such as 3.14.2.

program.description: The Program as analyzed: the learner's text as a file saved by a code editor, so it ends with a newline.

fileName.description: The name the Program was saved under for the Try it yourself commands, such as program.py.

bytes.description: The Program's bytes in UTF-8, in order: zoom level 2.

commands.description: Each Try it yourself command the browser's Python ran on the Program, and what it printed.

CommandRun.title: CommandRun
CommandRun.description: One Try it yourself command, run by the browser's Python on the Program saved as fileName.

command.description: The command, as the learner would type it: python program.py.

output.description: What a terminal shows: everything written to stdout and stderr, in the order it was written.

exitStatus.description: The command's exit status: 0 if it ended normally, 1 after an error, or the number passed to sys.exit.

id.description: Fact ID: byte-0 for the first byte, byte-1 for the next, and so on.

value.description: The byte, a number from 0 to 255.

charIndex.description: Which character of the program this byte encodes, counted in Unicode code points from 0. A character can take up to 4 bytes, which then share a charIndex.

line.description: The line the character is on, counted from 1. A line's newline belongs to that line.

Templates.title: Templates
Templates.description: The Templates for one Python version, in one file, such as templates/py314.json.

pythonVersion.description: The Python version the Templates explain, such as 3.14.

templates.description: Each Template, by its ID, such as byte.newline.

tryIt.description: Each zoom level's Try it yourself command, by level number. A level without one has no Try it yourself section.

TryIt.title: TryIt
TryIt.description: A zoom level's Try it yourself: a real command the learner can run on their own computer. Its strings are filled in like a Template whose subject is program.

command.description: The command, such as python {file}. The browser's Python runs it on the Program.

intro.description: What to do before typing the command.

parts.description: The What it does tab: each part of the command, and what it does.

read.description: The How to read it tab: notes on reading the output, after anything the page works out from the Program.

TryItPart.title: TryItPart
TryItPart.description: One part of a Try it yourself command.

code.description: The part, as it appears in the command; … stands for what is inside it.

Template.title: Template
Template.description: Stored explanation text for one kind of element, in one plain-English voice. Filling it in with Facts makes an Explanation. In its strings, {slot} is a Fact value of its subject, **words** are bold, and [[concept|words]] are words with a Concept card.

title.description: The Explanation's heading, if it has one.

term.description: The technical term, shown once in small print, such as code point U+0070.

Subject.title: Subject
Subject.description: What a Template explains, which decides its slots: program, the whole Program (ProgramSlot); byte, one ByteFact (ByteSlot); or line, one line of the Program (LineSlot).

LineSlot.title: LineSlot
LineSlot.description: A Fact about one line of the Program that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: How many spaces start the line, with the word: 4 spaces.
The line after those spaces, without its newline.

ProgramSlot.title: ProgramSlot
ProgramSlot.description: A Fact about the whole Program that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: How many lines, with the word: 1 line, 5 lines.
How many characters, counting spaces and newlines, with the word: 63 characters.
How many bytes, with the word: 22 bytes.
The name to save the Program under, for the Try it yourself commands: program.py.

ByteSlot.title: ByteSlot
ByteSlot.description: A Fact about one byte, and the character it encodes, that a Template can name.

oneOf.description: Which byte of the Program it is, counted from 1.
How many bytes the Program has, as a number.
The character it encodes, with a newline drawn as ↵, a space as ␠ and a tab as ⇥.
The line the character is on, counted from 1.
How many spaces indent that line, with the word: 4 spaces.
How many bytes the character takes, with the word: 2 bytes.
All the character's bytes, in order: 195 169.
Which of the character's bytes this is, as a word: first, second, third or fourth.

ConceptCards.title: ConceptCards
ConceptCards.description: Every Concept card, and the Concepts index that groups them: concepts/cards.json.

cards.description: Each Concept card, by its ID, such as utf8. Text refers to a card as [[utf8|words]].

index.description: The Concepts index: groups of cards, in order. Every card is in exactly one group.

ConceptCard.title: ConceptCard
ConceptCard.description: A short, self-contained explanation of a general computing idea. Its strings can hold **words** in bold and [[card|words]] that open another card.

name.description: The card's heading, such as UTF-8.

related.description: The IDs of related cards, shown as buttons that open them.

ConceptVisual.title: ConceptVisual
ConceptVisual.description: A picture under a card's text.

BitsVisual.title: BitsVisual
BitsVisual.description: The 8 bits of one byte, with each bit's value and their sum.

Utf8Visual.title: Utf8Visual
Utf8Visual.description: A table of characters and the UTF-8 bytes that store them. The page works the bytes out; the file only lists the characters.

HonestyLabelsVisual.title: HonestyLabelsVisual
HonestyLabelsVisual.description: Every Honesty label, with what it means. The card that shows it is the one every label chip opens.

ConceptGroup.title: ConceptGroup
ConceptGroup.description: One group in the Concepts index.

name.description: The group's heading, such as Storing text.

HonestyLabels.title: HonestyLabels
HonestyLabels.description: The set of Honesty labels, and which one each zoom level and panel carries: concepts/honesty-labels.json. Changing the set is an edit to this file alone.

labels.description: Each label, by its ID, in the order the How we know card lists them.

levels.description: The label each built zoom level carries, by level number. A level that isn't built yet has none.

panels.description: The label of each panel whose provenance differs from its level.

byteBits.description: Zoom level 2's panel How the number N is stored.

machineMap.description: The Machine map, beside every zoom level.

tryItOutput.description: Try it yourself's What you’ll see tab, when the browser's Python ran the command on the Program.

HonestyLabel.title: HonestyLabel
HonestyLabel.description: One Honesty label: how the content it is on knows what it shows.

name.description: The word on the chip, such as Observed.

means.description: What the label means, on the How we know card.

warning.description: Shown in the warning color. Only Illustrative is, and the build allows one label at most.
